newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurance firms' net doubles in H1 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurance firms' net doubles in H1 - survey.

text.p: Polish insurance companies earned 120.3 million zlotys in the first half of 1996, up from 53.8 million zlotys in the first half of 1995, but only 15 firms had profits while 17 showed losses, a survey by the Nowa Europa daily showed.
The survey showed the gross premiums of Polish insurers rose 44.6 percent to 4,318.7 million zlotys.
The gross premiums grew 53.4 percent in life-insurance sector and 41.1 percent in non-life insurances.

The Nowa Europa said state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) had 67.5 percent of the market share in non-life insurances while Warta had eight percent. Medium-sized private companies held smaller stakes.
In the life-insurance sector PZU-Life had 80-percent of the market, Commercial Union 10 percent and Amplico Life seven percent.
